chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “When one of you finishes the salat (prayer), let him raise his hands toward the heaven and be earnest in du'a (supplication).”
So Ibn Saba' said, “O Amir al-Mu'minin, is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not in every place?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Then why does he raise his hands toward the heaven?”
So he said, “Do you not recite: ‘And in the heaven is your sustenance and what you are promised’?”
Then from where should sustenance be sought except from its place? And the place of sustenance and what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has promised is the heaven.

key_terms.الدُّعَاءِ: supplication directed to Allah عزّ وجلّ
key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: the heaven, toward which the hands are raised in du'a
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat (prayer) after which this act of supplication is performed
key_terms.مَا تُوعَدُونَ: what you are promised by Allah عزّ وجلّ

ai.seo_question: Why should one raise the hands toward the heaven in du'a after salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the etiquette of du'a (supplication) after salat (prayer), including raising the hands toward the heaven. It explains this practice through the Qur'anic verse that places sustenance and the divine promise in the heaven, while affirming that Allah عزّ وجلّ is not confined by place.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.955 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"When one of you finishes the prayer, let him raise his hands to the sky and be earnest in supplication."
Ibn Saba asked: "O’ Commander of the Faithful, is not Allah (swt) present everywhere?"
He (Imam Ali) replied: "Indeed, He is."
Ibn Saba then asked: "So why do we raise our hands towards the sky?"
Imam Ali answered, "Do you not recite: '
And in the heaven is your sustenance and what you are promised' (Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:22)?
From where else should sustenance be sought except from its place, and the place of sustenance and Allah’s (swt) promise is in the sky."
